subject: 5074FD02BF4C47E68CE9773D10D7AB7C
introduction: When the Báb sent out his first eighteen disciples he told them to expect neither food nor reward from any city, and to shake its dust from their feet when they left. Detachment, in these fifteen readings, is the teacher’s freedom from three things: from needing support or thanks, from the world’s distractions and its clamour, and from the result. The last is stated by Bahá’u’lláh in one of his best-known counsels: if you possess a jewel of which others are deprived, share it “in a language of utmost kindliness and goodwill”; if it is refused, “leave him unto himself.” The Báb’s words deliberately recall the sending of the twelve in the Gospel, and the Gospel passages are placed beside them. The Qur’án has each prophet say “I ask of you no wage” and tells Muhammad that he is a reminder and not a warder; Paul worked with his hands so as to preach “without charge”; and the Gítá teaches action without attachment to its fruit.
questions: “In no wise expect either meat or reward.” What rewards, other than money, might a person look for in sharing a belief?
“If it be accepted … your object is attained. If anyone should refuse it, leave him unto himself.” Why is this hard, and what does it protect in the other person?
The Gítá says to act without regard for “the fruit.” How is that different from not caring whether one’s effort does any good?
The last reading warns against teaching someone out of affection for him, or for a benefit to oneself. What motive is left?

outside.why: The Báb’s charge to his first disciples: “in no wise expect either meat or reward.” It follows, almost word for word, the charge of Jesus: freely ye have received, freely give. Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses.
“When you depart out of that city, you should shake the dust from off your feet.” Jesus: whosoever shall not receive you, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.
The prophets of the Qur’án each say it to their people: I ask of you no wage therefor; my wage is the concern only of the Lord of the Worlds.
“Beware lest the affairs of the contingent world withhold thee from utterance.” Jesus to Martha: thou art careful and troubled about many things: but one thing is needful.
“The intention of the teacher must be pure, his heart independent.” Paul on his own motives: not as pleasing men, but God, which trieth our hearts; nor of men sought we glory.
Then his breath “will exert influence.” Whitman: I and mine do not convince by arguments, similes, rhymes, we convince by our presence.
“Suffer your intentions to work for the good of all; cut your attachment” from the world. Krishna to Arjuna: let right deeds be thy motive, not the fruit which comes from them.
“Grieve not on account of the people and their clamor.” Paul on whose business the result is: I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
Passing from city to city, “no dust settled upon our shoes.” Paul: when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge.
A teacher “must needs detach himself from all earthly things.” Paul: no man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life.
Teachers should travel on their own means, with “independence.” Paul to the elders of Ephesus: these hands have ministered unto my necessities, and to them that were with me.
“Forsaking home and comfort, become a wanderer.” Jesus to the seventy: carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes.
The teacher sanctifies himself from “all things of the world” and leaves the result. Ecclesiastes: cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.

Share a truth “in a language of utmost kindliness.” If it is refused, leave the person to himself. The Qur’án to its Prophet: remind them, for thou art but a remembrancer, thou art not at all a warder over them.

The Qur’án again: the guiding of them is not thy duty, but Allah guideth whom He will. A teacher who believes this is spared anxiety over results. Could he also be spared effort? How does the reading keep both the offering and the freedom?

quran-guiding-of-them-is-not-thy-duty.text: The guiding of them is not thy duty (O Muhammad), but Allah guideth whom He will. And whatsoever good thing ye spend, it is for yourselves, when ye spend not save in search of Allah's Countenance; and whatsoever good thing ye spend, it will be repaid to you in full, and ye will not be wronged.

corinthians-gospel-without-charge.text: What is my reward then? Verily that, when I preach the gospel, I may make the gospel of Christ without charge, that I abuse not my power in the gospel

thessalonians-not-as-pleasing-men.text: But as we were allowed of God to be put in trust with the gospel, even so we speak; not as pleasing men, but God, which trieth our hearts. For neither at any time used we flattering words, as ye know, nor a cloke of covetousness; God is witness: Nor of men sought we glory, neither of you, nor yet of others, when we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ

matthew-freely-ye-have-received.text: freely ye have received, freely give. Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses, Nor scrip for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his meat
